references.text: Moses uses the same argument that the nations will hear about Israel's destruction and draw negative conclusions about God's power
Moses asks that God not destroy the people because the neighboring nations will say that the Lord was unable to bring them into the promised land
God's concern that enemies will misinterpret His actions toward Israel
Joshua uses a similar argument about what the peoples will say regarding God's name if Israel is wiped out
God's care for His name among the nations and how they will perceive His actions
Reference to Moses who stood in the gap for the people to avert destruction
The Lord's threat to strike the people with plague and wipe them out, which Moses' prayer addresses
